"Goal/Purpose": "Expand the Panama Canal PIEA to promote sustainable land-use management in the Panama Canal watershed and support implementation of relevant objectives and targets of the Indicative Environmental Land-Use Plan for the Panama Canal Watershed (PIOTA–CHCP).",
"Action/Intervention": "Expand the Panama Canal PIEA through the PBP Agreement, leveraging the PIEA incentive model to ensure performance-based implementation; provide a package of incentives targeting small scale producers and local communities, including equitably women and men among them; foster conservation and restoration of prioritized forest ecosystems; implement sustainable agriculture packages, including agro-forestry and silvopastoral systems; support family agriculture and alternative livelihoods; and expand the Conservation PES Programme in the Panama Canal watershed.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Panama Canal watershed, including prioritized forest ecosystems in the basin.",
"Target Audience": "Small scale producers and local communities, including equitably women and men among them; ACP.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Sustainable land-use management in the Panama Canal watershed; conservation and restoration of prioritized forest ecosystems; implementation of sustainable agriculture packages, including agro-forestry and silvopastoral systems; support for family agriculture and alternative livelihoods; expansion of the Conservation PES Programme; and support for implementation of relevant objectives and targets of PIOTA–CHCP related to territorial and environmental management, ecosystems and protected areas, decarbonization, climate resilience, and sustainable land-use in the basin."

"Target Audience": "Not explicitly specified.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Implementation of the PIEA package of incentives outside the Panama Canal watershed, guided by relevant PIOTAs and supported by an institutional and management structure, under a socially inclusive and gender-responsive approach."
panama_CNR_3:
"Goal/Purpose": "To develop the institutional and management structure to implement a socially inclusive and gender-responsive incentives program targeting Indigenous Peoples, Afro Descendant communities, and small-scale producers, tailored to their specific socio-economic characteristics, relationship with forest ecosystems, and traditional knowledge, and linked to measurable outcomes.",
"Action/Intervention": "Implement an incentives Programme that includes instruments to stimulate the conservation and sustainable management of forests; management and sustainable use of non-timber forest products (NTFP); livelihood activities compatible with protected area management, including community nurseries for native seedlings, value chains for NTFP such as honey, seeds, fibers, and handicrafts, and low-impact ecotourism activities such as guiding, trails, and signage; ensure all activities are aligned with protected area zoning and management plans; and design and implement the program following the PBP logic, linking payments to measurable outcomes.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Forest ecosystems and protected areas (PA), including activities related to non-timber forest products.",
"Target Audience": "Indigenous Peoples, Afro Descendant communities, and small-scale producers, including women and men among them.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Conservation and sustainable management of forests; sustainable use and management of non-timber forest products; promotion of conservation efforts through livelihoods compatible with protected area management; environmental integrity and sustainability; and payments linked to measurable outcomes."

"Action/Intervention": "Financing the National Restoration Programme; enriching secondary forests; promoting native regeneration and reforestation with native species; fostering ecosystem connectivity through biological corridors; increasing nursery production; enhancing carbon stocks through ecological restoration in protected areas and their buffer zones; strengthening effective management; improving landscape connectivity by establishing biological corridors; promoting Other Effective Area-Based Conservation Measures (OECMs) in buffer zones; aligning all interventions with protected area zoning and management plans.",

panama_HR_1:
"Goal/Purpose": "Prioritize, implement, track, adjust, and institutionalize mitigation policies and measures by sector to contribute to GHG reduction, strengthen coordination and planning coherence, and ensure continuity of implemented mitigation measures beyond 2035.",
"Action/Intervention": "Define a prioritized portfolio of sectoral policies and measures with institutional leads, time horizon, and indicative contribution to GHG reduction using updated GHG projections; strengthen the use of ReNAM within the National Climate Transparency Platform for registration and tracking of mitigation actions through technical guidelines, accompaniment, and inter-institutional coordination agreements; analyze the technical, institutional, and economic feasibility of main mitigation measures to prioritize those with greatest short- and medium-term implementation potential and define execution paths; establish formal inter-institutional coordination mechanisms for mitigation implementation with agreed roles, responsibilities, and information flows; implement pilot mitigation projects and programs in prioritized sectors (energy, waste, agriculture, and industrial processes); formalize implementation agreements with sectoral entities and key actors defining commitments, technical roles, and tracking mechanisms; provide technical accompaniment to sectoral entities for launching prioritized mitigation measures; activate existing or under-development economic and financial instruments to support execution of viable mitigation measures, including incentives, climate finance, and market mechanisms when relevant; adjust the mitigation-measures portfolio based on observed results; adjust economic incentives, institutional arrangements, and technical guidelines to facilitate sustained adoption of scalable mitigation measures in coordination with Target 14; strengthen coherence between mitigation, sectoral planning, and territorial planning so new public and private investments consider GHG-reduction criteria aligned with this target; review the national emissions-reduction trajectory against the required trajectory to identify gaps and guide corrective decisions; reinforce inter-institutional coordination to close gaps by concentrating efforts on actions with greatest contribution potential; consolidate implemented mitigation measures within permanent sectoral and climate planning instruments.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Climate mitigation; sectoral and territorial planning; National Climate Transparency Platform/ReNAM; prioritized sectors: energy, waste, agriculture, and industrial processes.",
"Target Audience": "Sectoral entities involved in mitigation implementation, institutional leads, key actors, and inter-institutional coordination bodies.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "A prioritized and feasible mitigation portfolio is defined and implemented; mitigation actions are registered and tracked through ReNAM; pilot projects are launched in prioritized sectors; implementation agreements and coordination mechanisms are formalized; economic and financial instruments are activated to support viable measures; mitigation measures are adjusted based on results; coherence is strengthened between mitigation, sectoral planning, and territorial planning; gaps in the national emissions-reduction trajectory are identified and addressed; and implemented mitigation measures are consolidated in permanent planning instruments to ensure continuity beyond 2035."
panama_HR_2:
{
  "Goal/Purpose": "Update and execute the National Forest Restoration Program at scale, with measurable progress toward restoring 100,000 ha total, including 2,500 ha of mangrove and 25,000 ha of agricultural landscapes, while ensuring effective conservation, preventing unplanned agricultural expansion that implies forest conversion within corridors, improving productivity on prioritized farms, and achieving verifiable LULUCF accounting of at least 1 million tCO₂e.",
  "Action/Intervention": "Validate a national baseline quantifying and characterizing restorable degraded areas, areas to be placed under effective conservation, and farms and agricultural landscapes eligible for productive restoration; disaggregate the target into quantitative pathways and define gaps, priority territories, and preliminary annual targets by type; delimit and validate the Azuero, Coclé, and Veraguas corridors, approve functional zoning, and define land-use rules and intervention priorities; define effective-conservation guidelines for restored areas, including conservation agreements with landowners, community co-management where applicable, surveillance and compliance mechanisms, and management leads, and integrate these into SINAP/OECM as appropriate or equivalent conservation arrangements in productive landscapes; reorient agricultural programs and incentives to implement silvopastoral and agroforestry systems on prioritized farms, with productive-performance targets of at least 20% productivity increase and eligibility criteria linked to corridor zoning and non-conversion of forests; define and launch an operational mechanism to eliminate unplanned agricultural expansion implying forest conversion within corridors through municipal land-use planning and zoning guidelines, land-use-change traceability with satellite monitoring, and inter-institutionally coordinated control and compliance measures; design, implement, and monitor a traceability system for restoration actions aligned with existing national systems and national and international reporting requirements; approve an intervention plan for restoration of 2,500 ha of mangrove, including site selection, permits, agreements with communities/users, technical execution, and post-restoration protection and monitoring; execute the program with explicit annual targets, prioritizing interventions by corridor and ensuring each intervention has an associated effective-conservation instrument; implement silvopastoral/agroforestry systems through agricultural extension with technical assistance, access to inputs, and productive follow-up; operationalize the zero-unplanned-expansion mechanism through periodic land-cover-change monitoring, territorial early warnings, coordinated corrective measures, and semi-annual reports by corridor with public/administrative traceability; strengthen and evaluate conservation arrangements and adjust incentives and management rules according to corridor performance; adjust the restoration portfolio to prioritize interventions with greater carbon performance and permanence, ensuring verifiable LULUCF accounting consistent with the national reporting system; carry out verification integrating hectares restored by type, demonstrable effective conservation, productivity increase on intervened farms, compliance with zero unplanned expansion in corridors, and LULUCF accounting.",

  "Target Audience": "National Forest Restoration Program implementers; landowners; communities/users; management leads; agricultural programs and extension services; prioritized farms; municipalities; inter-institutional authorities responsible for control and compliance; and national systems responsible for conservation integration, monitoring, traceability, and reporting.",
  "Expected Impact/Outcome": "A validated national baseline and quantified pathways for restoration; approved corridor delimitation, zoning, land-use rules, and intervention priorities; effective-conservation arrangements established for restored areas; implementation of silvopastoral and agroforestry systems on prioritized farms with at least 20% productivity increase; an operational mechanism eliminating unplanned agricultural expansion that implies forest conversion within corridors; a functioning traceability and monitoring system for restoration actions; an approved and implemented mangrove restoration plan covering 2,500 ha; measurable progress toward restoring 100,000 ha total, including 25,000 ha of agricultural landscapes; reduced risks of reversal in restored areas; semi-annual corridor reports and public/administrative traceability; and verification of hectares restored by type, effective conservation, farm productivity increase, compliance with zero unplanned expansion, and LULUCF accounting of at least 1 million tCO₂e."
}
panama_HR_3:
"Goal/Purpose": "Ensure minimum standards of effective conservation in SINAP; expand SINAP to 40% terrestrial and 60% marine; strengthen effective conservation inside and outside formal protected areas through OECM and complementary arrangements; align the National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan as an enabling instrument of the Nature Pledge; develop integrated management in 10 strategic watersheds; guarantee coherence among conservation, land-use planning, local development, and cultural safeguards; and incorporate effective management of SINAP and OECM permanently into national, budgetary, and sectoral planning instruments beyond 2035.",
"Action/Intervention": "Review and update the regulatory, normative, and operational framework of SINAP; carry out a national diagnosis of effective management of terrestrial, marine, and continental protected areas, identifying gaps in planning, financing, personnel, control, monitoring, and community participation; define a technical roadmap for SINAP expansion to 40% terrestrial and 60% marine, prioritizing areas of high ecological value, connectivity, and climate resilience and incorporating criteria of effective-management feasibility and sustainable financing before new declarations; identify, evaluate, and recognize OECM and complementary arrangements in indigenous, private, and community territories and integrate them into the national conservation system; update and align the NBSAP with the Nature Pledge's governance, financing, incentives, and information-management frameworks; select and prioritize 10 strategic watersheds for integrated management plans; strengthen SINAP's operational capacities through investment in personnel, equipment, control and surveillance, and co-management mechanisms; develop, approve, and implement integrated management plans in the 10 priority watersheds with clear zoning, control mechanisms, community participation, and alignment with municipal and sectoral plans; channel permanent financing for SINAP management through the Fondo Panamá Natural and other mechanisms; periodically evaluate management effectiveness of protected areas and OECM using ecological, social, and governance indicators and adjust management plans, institutional arrangements, and resource allocation according to results; guarantee articulation among SINAP, indigenous territories, and local governments; verify compliance with coverage goals and effective management of SINAP and OECM, including ecological performance, governance, and financial sustainability; incorporate effective management of SINAP and OECM permanently into national, budgetary, and sectoral planning instruments.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "SINAP (National System of Protected Areas); terrestrial, marine, and continental protected areas; OECM and complementary conservation arrangements; indigenous, private, and community territories; 10 strategic watersheds; areas of high ecological value; municipal, sectoral, national, budgetary, and land-use planning domains.",
"Target Audience": "SINAP; protected areas and OECM managers; indigenous territories; private and community territories; local governments; municipal and sectoral planning authorities; Fondo Panamá Natural; institutions responsible for the NBSAP and the Nature Pledge.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Minimum standards of effective conservation established; national diagnosis of management gaps completed; technical roadmap for expansion to 40% terrestrial and 60% marine defined; OECM and complementary arrangements recognized and integrated into the national conservation system; NBSAP updated and aligned with the Nature Pledge; 10 strategic watersheds selected and prioritized and integrated management plans developed, approved, and implemented; strengthened operational capacities of SINAP; permanent financing channeled for operation, monitoring, and compliance; periodic evaluation of management effectiveness conducted and management adjusted according to results; coherence ensured among conservation, land-use planning, local development, and cultural safeguards; compliance with coverage and effective-management goals verified; and effective management of SINAP and OECM incorporated permanently into national, budgetary, and sectoral planning instruments beyond 2035."
panama_HR_4:
"Goal/Purpose": "Strengthen conservation and management of priority native species and human-wildlife conflict management through updated prioritization, identification of critical conflict areas, implementation of management measures, institutional formalization, monitoring, territorial scaling, and permanent updating mechanisms.",
"Action/Intervention": "Update and validate a national list of priority native species for conservation using criteria of extinction risk, ecological value, territorial distribution, and level of human-wildlife conflict, with focus on species whose loss would have systemic effects; identify and delimit five critical areas of human-wildlife conflict and analyze causes, actors involved, socio-economic impacts, and existing institutional capacities; implement human-wildlife conflict management measures in prioritized critical areas, including prevention protocols, compensation, risk management, and strengthening local capacities for coexistence; review the institutional base and verify the need to establish a monitoring system for priority species and human-wildlife conflicts, integrating indicators of population status, genetic diversity, and reduction of incidents, interoperable with national environmental information systems; scale up species-management and human-wildlife coexistence approaches to new priority territories, strengthening articulation with SINAP management plans, biological corridors, and productive landscapes; formalize national protocols for management of priority species and human-wildlife conflicts through administrative and technical instruments of MiAMBIENTE, defining institutional responsibilities, activation criteria, inter-institutional coordination mechanisms, and territorial application guidelines; integrate priority-species conservation and human-wildlife conflict management programs into the regular operational plans of SINAP and the biodiversity and wildlife directorates, ensuring annual planning, recurrent budget allocation, and continuous technical follow-up; establish a permanent mechanism for updating priority species and critical conflict areas based on scientific evidence and continuous monitoring, allowing periodic adjustment of management priorities without creating new policies or regulatory frameworks.",

"Target Audience": "MiAMBIENTE, SINAP, the biodiversity and wildlife directorates, institutions involved in inter-institutional coordination, local capacities in prioritized critical areas, and stakeholders involved in human-wildlife conflict areas.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "A validated national list of priority native species; identification and delimitation of five critical human-wildlife conflict areas; implementation of prevention, compensation, risk management, and coexistence measures in prioritized areas; reviewed institutional base and verification of the need for a monitoring system with indicators on population status, genetic diversity, and incident reduction; scaled-up species-management and coexistence approaches in new priority territories; formalized national protocols with defined responsibilities and coordination mechanisms; integration of programs into regular operational plans with annual planning, recurrent budget allocation, and continuous technical follow-up; and a permanent evidence-based mechanism for periodic updating of priority species and critical conflict areas."
panama_HR_5:
"Goal/Purpose": "Control illegal wildlife trafficking through prioritized regional action, inter-institutional coordination, personnel training, strengthened legal and sustainable trade controls, integrated information systems, continuous evaluation and adjustment of mechanisms, stable resource allocation, and consolidation of a national case registration, analysis, and follow-up system that incorporates zoonotic-risk and conservation criteria.",
"Action/Intervention": "Identify and prioritize at least five regions with high incidence of illegal wildlife trafficking; establish inter-institutional operational coordination protocols among MiAMBIENTE, MINSA, Customs, and security agencies; train park rangers, health personnel, and security forces in species identification, safe handling of seized wildlife, and zoonotic-risk prevention; implement coordinated and permanent control operations in prioritized regions; strengthen control mechanisms for legal and sustainable trade of species, including traceability and permit compliance and respect for traditional uses of indigenous peoples and local communities; integrate operational and control information into national environmental and risk-information systems; evaluate effectiveness of control mechanisms and coordination; adjust protocols, administrative procedures, and regulatory frameworks based on lessons learned and newly identified threats; define and ensure stable allocation of human, logistical, and operational resources in institutional budgets and operational plans; consolidate a national interoperable system for registration, analysis, and follow-up of illegal wildlife trafficking cases and zoonotic-risk events.",

"Expected Impact/Outcome": "At least five high-incidence regions prioritized; operational coordination protocols established; field and control personnel trained; coordinated and permanent control operations implemented in prioritized regions; strengthened traceability and permit compliance in legal and sustainable species trade; information integrated into national systems for analysis of trends, routes, and effectiveness; effectiveness of mechanisms and coordination evaluated and gaps identified; protocols, procedures, and regulatory frameworks adjusted; stable resource allocation integrated into institutional budgets and plans; a national interoperable system established for monitoring illegal wildlife trafficking cases, zoonotic-risk events, trends, routes, and effectiveness of control measures."
panama_HR_6:

panama_HR_7:
"Goal/Purpose": "By 2035, Panama will reduce pollution and its cumulative effects by reducing by at least 50% the excess nutrients released into the environment and the risks associated with the use of pesticides, fungicides, and hazardous chemicals, complemented by a significant increase in the adoption of clean technologies in productive sectors.",
"Action/Intervention": "Prioritize a limited set of watersheds and critical territories where pollution by nutrients and chemicals represents greater environmental, health, or economic risks; identify the national technological gap for the reduction of pollution by chemicals and nutrients and map clean technologies available internationally that are not yet present or widespread in Panama; define a national pathway for the progressive reduction of risks from chemicals and nutrients, with clear milestones at 2030 and 2035, identifying priority sectors, types of instruments to be used, and expected levels of intervention, without yet initiating implementation at the national scale; align the chemicals- and nutrients-reduction pathway with the analysis of perverse and positive incentives in Target 14, identifying polluting practices currently incentivized and technical alternatives that require economic or other incentives for their adoption; design very focused pilot interventions in one or two prioritized territories to test combinations of technical assistance, incentive adjustments, and institutional arrangements for the reduction of pollutant loads; implement integrated territorial interventions in the prioritized watersheds and productive zones, combining the progressive reduction of the use of polluting inputs, integrated nutrient management, and the adoption of practices and technologies of lower environmental impact; technically accompany producers, agro-industries, and industrial actors in the transition toward less polluting productive practices; apply in the intervened territories the economic incentives and technical support prioritized under Target 14; scale up the adoption of clean technologies and low-impact nutrient-management practices to new territories and productive sectors, prioritizing those with the greatest contribution to pollution and with demonstrated enabling conditions; focus additional actions on the territories or sectors that still present elevated levels of pollution by chemicals and nutrients, reinforcing combinations of clean technologies, incentives, and environmental control.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Prioritized watersheds, critical territories, intervened territories, marine-coastal, restoration-related territories, productive zones, productive sectors, agro-industries, and industrial sectors in Panama.",
"Target Audience": "Panama; producers; agro-industries; industrial actors; productive sectors.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "At least 50% reduction in excess nutrients released into the environment by 2035; reduced risks associated with the use of pesticides, fungicides, and hazardous chemicals; significant increase in the adoption of clean technologies in productive sectors; progressive reduction of pollutant loads; adoption of low-impact nutrient-management practices; reinforced action in territories or sectors that still present elevated levels of pollution by chemicals and nutrients."

panama_HR_9:
"Goal/Purpose": "Update, harmonize, and strengthen Panama’s legal, administrative, policy, and institutional frameworks for access to genetic resources, DSI, FPIC, and benefit-sharing, ensuring coherence with the CBD, the Nagoya Protocol, the Cali Fund, international standards, and the Panamanian constitutional framework.",
"Action/Intervention": "Carry out a comparative legal analysis on frameworks for access to genetic resources, DSI, and benefit-sharing; identify existing legal, administrative, and policy frameworks in Panama that require updating or harmonization; evaluate the actual functioning of the existing system through review of contracts, agreed and delivered benefits, processing times, and compliance with FPIC in previous experiences; design participatory national guidelines for FPIC considering gender equity and in coordination with indigenous peoples and local communities; strengthen technical and institutional capacities in competent entities for management, compliance monitoring, and benefit negotiation; approve a legal and administrative framework that establishes mandatory review procedures for new laws and policies, creates the National Registry of Applications and Contracts, defines the benefit-sharing mechanism, adopts official contract templates, and establishes periodic compliance audits with mandatory application from 2028 onward; institutionalize permanent dialogue processes with indigenous peoples and local communities; establish clear procedures for benefit management including agreements, funds, or redistribution mechanisms; implement national monitoring and reporting mechanisms.",

"Target Audience": "Competent entities in Panama; indigenous peoples and local communities; stakeholders involved in the governance, management, monitoring, and benefit-sharing of genetic resources.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Updated and harmonized frameworks incorporating DSI, FPIC, and benefit-sharing mechanisms; participatory national FPIC guidelines; strengthened technical and institutional capacities; establishment of the National Registry of Applications and Contracts, official contract templates, benefit-sharing mechanisms, periodic compliance audits, and permanent dialogue processes; clear procedures for benefit management; national monitoring and reporting mechanisms; mandatory application of the approved framework from 2028 onward; and at least 80% of the relevant new frameworks fully complying with the Nagoya Protocol and the Cali Fund."
panama_HR_10:
"Goal/Purpose": "Identify and prioritize productive sectors and consumption patterns with the greatest environmental, material, and climate footprint, and progressively establish, implement, strengthen, expand, and integrate corporate commitments on sustainable production and consumption, ensuring credibility, traceability, coherence with enabling instruments, and alignment with circular economy, waste reduction, and efficient resource use targets.",
"Action/Intervention": "Identify and prioritize sectors and consumption patterns with the greatest footprint; design a framework of gradual corporate commitments with progressive levels of ambition differentiated by sector and priority areas; define minimum credibility and traceability criteria for corporate commitments, including acceptable types of action and minimum required evidence; establish an articulation pathway between corporate commitments and economic, financial, and regulatory instruments; install a mechanism of structured dialogue with high-impact companies and strategic sectoral actors; progressively implement prioritized corporate commitments and accompany high-impact companies in adopting sustainable production and consumption practices; strengthen technical and management capacities in high-impact companies; selectively apply enabled economic and financial instruments to incentivize compliance; strengthen performance requirements associated with corporate commitments over time; expand adoption of corporate commitments to more high-impact companies and sectors; close persistent gaps in lagging sectors or companies through regulation, differentiated incentives, and corrective measures; integrate adopted commitments and practices into monitoring, reporting, and public-private dialogue mechanisms.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Productive sectors and consumption patterns with the greatest environmental, material, and climate footprint; priority areas including circular economy, waste reduction, and efficiency in resource use.",
"Target Audience": "High-impact companies; strategic sectoral actors; prioritized sectors and companies with the greatest potential for environmental impact and market transformation; lagging sectors or companies.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "A validated and progressively implemented framework of credible and traceable corporate commitments on sustainable production and consumption; strengthened technical and management capacities in high-impact companies; incentivized compliance through economic and financial instruments; increased technical and outcome demands over time; expanded adoption of commitments across more high-impact companies and sectors; closure of persistent gaps in lagging sectors or companies; and stable integration of commitments and practices into monitoring, reporting, and public-private dialogue mechanisms."
panama_HR_11:
"Goal/Purpose": "Design, validate, and expand a standardized national methodology for the characterization of urban solid waste and food waste; consolidate the resulting data into an official national baseline; establish that baseline as a mandatory reference for policy and measure design; and use the information to prioritize territorial and sectoral interventions for waste and food-waste reduction.",
"Action/Intervention": "Design and validate a standardized national methodology aligned with international standards and adaptable to diverse municipal contexts; select representative municipalities and execute pilot studies for the characterization of waste and food waste; ensure methodological consistency and collect data disaggregated by type of waste, source, and territory; train municipal technical teams, waste operators, and key actors in applying the methodology; expand the methodology nationally, prioritizing municipalities with greater waste generation and critical food-waste flows; consolidate collected data into an official national baseline integrated into national environmental information systems; publish and institutionally validate the national baseline; establish its use as a mandatory reference for the design of policies, incentives, and waste- and food-waste-reduction measures; use the information generated to prioritize territorial and sectoral interventions in coherence with Targets 10 and 12.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Urban solid waste and food waste characterization, municipal contexts, and national environmental information systems.",
"Target Audience": "Municipal technical teams, waste operators, key actors involved in methodology application, representative municipalities, municipalities with greater waste generation and critical food-waste flows, and institutions responsible for national environmental information systems and policy design.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "A standardized and validated national methodology for waste and food-waste characterization; pilot studies implemented in representative municipalities; trained actors with minimum capacities for future replication; national expansion of methodology application; an official national baseline on the generation and composition of urban solid waste and food waste integrated into national environmental information systems; institutional validation and publication of the baseline; mandatory use of the baseline as a reference for policies, incentives, and reduction measures; and prioritized territorial and sectoral interventions for waste and food-waste reduction."
panama_HR_12:
"Goal/Purpose": "Reduce mismanaged plastic pollution in Panama by 50% by 2035 through the progressive elimination of single-use plastics, strengthening the circular economy and recycling infrastructure.",
"Action/Intervention": "Operationalize the National Plastics Action Roadmap by prioritizing high-impact and high-early-feasibility interventions for implementation between 2026 and 2030; establish clear institutional arrangements for implementation among MiAMBIENTE, municipalities, the private sector, waste managers, and base recyclers; prepare enabling conditions including operational schemes for differentiated collection, classification, and valorization of plastic waste and mechanisms for articulation with existing or under-development economic instruments and incentives; implement prioritized interventions in defined territories with emphasis on reducing mismanaged plastic pollution; apply economic and public-policy instruments that disincentivize problematic plastic waste generation and favor source reduction, reuse, and valorization; monitor and report reduction of mismanaged plastic pollution using indicators, baselines, and methodologies established in the Plastics Roadmap and integrate them with national environmental information systems; scale up effective interventions to new territories while strengthening local governments' capacity; adjust regulatory, administrative, and operational frameworks related to plastics management based on implementation evidence and coherence with international commitments including the Global Plastics Treaty; strengthen markets for valorized plastic materials by promoting demand stability, quality of recovered materials, and economic sustainability of recycling and reuse chains; identify territories, waste streams, or types of plastics that continue to generate high levels of pollution and design specific corrective interventions combining operational adjustments, incentives, and environmental control; reinforce the application of existing economic and regulatory instruments to disincentivize practices that perpetuate plastic pollution.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Plastics management, waste management, circular economy, recycling infrastructure, and national environmental information systems in Panama.",
"Target Audience": "MiAMBIENTE, municipalities, the private sector, waste managers, base recyclers, local governments, and actors involved in recycling and reuse chains.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "A 50% reduction in mismanaged plastic pollution by 2035; progressive elimination of single-use plastics; strengthened differentiated collection, classification, and valorization of plastic waste; implementation of prioritized interventions in defined territories and their scale-up to new territories; improved coherence with the legal framework on waste and plastics and international commitments; stronger markets for valorized plastic materials; and monitoring and reporting of pollution reduction through established indicators, baselines, and methodologies."
panama_HR_13:
"Goal/Purpose": "Establish and operationalize a coherent national biosafety framework in Panama for the evaluation, authorization, control, follow-up, and safe management of living modified organisms and biotechnology, with inter-institutional coordination, traceability, periodic updating, and coherence with access and fair benefit-sharing and FPIC when genetic resources or traditional knowledge are involved.",
"Action/Intervention": "Carry out an exhaustive mapping of competencies, current procedures, and regulatory gaps in biosafety; identify which institution evaluates risks, authorizes, oversees, controls imports, manages incidents, and administers information related to living modified organisms and biotechnology; define and formalize through an administrative act a mechanism of inter-institutional coordination on biosafety among MiAMBIENTE, MINSA, MIDA, AUPSA, and Customs; develop a technical document for a National Biosafety Strategy that consolidates the existing framework, sets operational objectives, prioritizes biotechnology-related risks relevant to Panama, and defines a limited set of concrete measures of safe management to be implemented before 2030; adopt and operationalize standardized procedures for risk assessment and authorization of biotechnological activities, including forms, technical criteria, response times, and clearly defined institutional responsibilities; implement at least five specific measures for the safe management of biotechnology; operationally integrate the principles of access and fair benefit-sharing and FPIC into biosafety procedures when genetic resources or traditional knowledge are involved; establish a national system for the registration and traceability of authorized biotechnological activities interoperable with environmental and transparency information systems; strengthen the operational capacity of competent institutions for oversight and control in territory through inspection protocols, information exchange, and coordination among environmental, health, and customs authorities; establish a permanent technical procedure for the periodic updating of biosafety measures to incorporate new technologies, emerging risks, and lessons learned.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Biosafety; biotechnology; living modified organisms; genetic resources and traditional knowledge where involved; environmental, health, customs, and transparency information systems in Panama.",
"Target Audience": "MiAMBIENTE, MINSA, MIDA, AUPSA, Customs, and other competent institutions responsible for biosafety evaluation, authorization, oversight, control, incident management, information administration, inspection, and coordination.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "An exhaustive mapping of competencies, procedures, and regulatory gaps completed; a formal inter-institutional coordination mechanism established; a technical document for a National Biosafety Strategy developed; standardized procedures for risk assessment and authorization adopted and operationalized; at least five specific safe management measures implemented before 2030; access and fair benefit-sharing and FPIC integrated into biosafety procedures when applicable; a national registration and traceability system established and interoperable with environmental and transparency information systems; strengthened institutional operational capacity for territorial oversight and control; and a permanent technical procedure established for periodic updating of biosafety measures."
panama_HR_14:
"Goal/Purpose": "To review incentives and subsidies with direct or indirect impact on biodiversity, evaluate and prioritize harmful incentives, reform or eliminate prioritized harmful incentives, redirect resources toward positive incentives for biodiversity, increase positive incentives, integrate biodiversity criteria into new incentives and subsidies, and ensure transparency and follow-up through publication and periodic updates of the inventory and status of incentives.",
"Action/Intervention": "Exhaustively review the analysis of incentives and subsidies (fiscal, financial, budgetary, and regulatory) with direct or indirect impact on biodiversity, including productive sectors, energy, transport, land use, and fisheries; adopt an official methodology for the evaluation of biodiversity impacts, aligned with international standards, to classify incentives as harmful, neutral, or positive, incorporating environmental, social, and economic criteria; evaluate and prioritize the most critical harmful incentives, considering magnitude of impact, irreversibility, affected groups, and feasibility of reform; design an incentives-reform roadmap that includes progressive elimination, redesign, or substitution by positive incentives, incorporating fiscal, social, and territorial analysis; establish an inter-institutional mechanism for dialogue and consultation, ensuring fair and effective processes with productive sectors, local governments, indigenous peoples, civil society, and the private sector; implement the elimination or reform of at least 50% of the prioritized harmful incentives through regulatory, fiscal, or administrative adjustments, ensuring transition measures for affected sectors; redirect resources released toward positive incentives for biodiversity, including payments for ecosystem services, incentives for restoration, sustainable production, community conservation, and management of protected areas; increase by at least 30% the volume and scope of positive incentives, prioritizing strategic territories (corridors, watersheds, coastal zones) and vulnerable populations; integrate biodiversity criteria into new incentives and subsidies, avoiding the creation of future harmful incentives; publish and periodically update the inventory and status of incentives, guaranteeing transparency and follow-up of compliance with the target.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Biodiversity; productive sectors, energy, transport, land use, fisheries; strategic territories including corridors, watersheds, and coastal zones; protected areas.",
"Target Audience": "Productive sectors, local governments, indigenous peoples, civil society, the private sector, affected sectors, vulnerable populations.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Official methodology adopted for biodiversity impact evaluation of incentives; harmful, neutral, and positive incentives classified; most critical harmful incentives evaluated and prioritized; incentives-reform roadmap designed; inter-institutional dialogue and consultation mechanism established; at least 50% of prioritized harmful incentives eliminated or reformed; resources redirected toward positive incentives for biodiversity; volume and scope of positive incentives increased by at least 30%; biodiversity criteria integrated into new incentives and subsidies; inventory and status of incentives published and periodically updated with transparency and compliance follow-up."
panama_HR_15:
"Goal/Purpose": "Delimit and prioritize critical territories of illegal deforestation to focus actions of control, restoration, productive reconversion, prevention, follow-up, and reduction of illegal deforestation through coordinated territorial strategies and sustainable landscape management.",
"Action/Intervention": "Use forest-monitoring information and territorial analysis to prioritize critical territories; agree on an inter-institutional approach for control of illegal deforestation among MiAMBIENTE, MIDA, local authorities, and territorial actors; integrate sustainable productive alternatives into forest landscapes, including silvopastoral systems, agroforestry, and sustainable forest management; identify and prioritize economic and non-economic incentives for forest conservation and sustainable landscape management; strengthen the articulation between forest monitoring and decision-making so forest-cover-change information feeds early prevention and control actions; implement integrated territorial actions combining control of illegal deforestation, technical-productive accompaniment, and access to incentives; accompany producers and local communities in adopting sustainable productive practices with continuous technical assistance and articulation with existing sectoral programs; channel available financing and incentive mechanisms toward territories and actors adopting sustainable management and effective forest conservation; follow up on changes in deforestation dynamics using the national monitoring system; adjust territorial strategies based on observed results; expand effective territorial control in critical forest landscapes through continuous forest monitoring, institutional presence, and early-response mechanisms to illegal-deforestation alerts; formally integrate the reduction of illegal deforestation into agricultural planning and land-use planning instruments so new productive expansions are oriented exclusively to suitable and non-forested areas; strengthen long-term economic arrangements for conservation and sustainable forest management with continuity, clear rules, and sufficient coverage; consolidate and expand adoption of sustainable productive alternatives in prioritized territories with permanent technical assistance; focus intensive interventions on the last hotspots of illegal deforestation; reinforce deterrent and corrective measures against illegal deforestation, ensuring coherence among monitoring, oversight, and administrative sanction.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Critical territories of illegal deforestation, prioritized landscapes, critical forest landscapes, forest landscapes, intervened territories, hotspots of illegal deforestation, agricultural planning, and land-use planning.",
"Target Audience": "MiAMBIENTE, MIDA, local authorities, territorial actors, competent entities, local governments, producers, and local communities.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Coordinated prevention, control, and follow-up in prioritized areas; adoption and expansion of sustainable productive practices compatible with conservation; access to incentives and financing for sustainable management and forest conservation; early prevention and control actions informed by forest-cover monitoring; evaluation of effectiveness through changes in deforestation dynamics in intervened territories; reinforcement of strategies that show greater impact; orientation of new productive expansions exclusively to suitable and non-forested areas; continuity and sufficient coverage of incentives and financial mechanisms; reduction of illegal deforestation, including in residual hotspots; and coherence among monitoring, oversight, and administrative sanction."
panama_HR_16:
"Goal/Purpose": "Build and adopt a national operational definition of organic soils for public policy and MRV purposes; develop the national baseline of organic soils and associated wetlands; design and implement an operational package for conservation and sustainable management; establish effective-conservation mechanisms and territorial programs; operationalize monitoring and verification; scale up protection/management and productive practices; integrate protection and soil-carbon criteria into territorial and productive planning; and verify progress toward 70% of organic soils under effective protection/management and +10% soil organic carbon in prioritized agricultural lands and grasslands.",
"Action/Intervention": "Agree on technical identification criteria for peatlands, wetlands, and high-carbon soils and a minimum protocol for data collection and validation; consolidate existing information and fill priority gaps through validation in critical territories, including preliminary delimitation and prioritization by risk and carbon/biodiversity value; define intermediate targets for 2030-2033, institutional responsibilities, adoption mechanism with MIDA and IDIAP, and incentives and financing pathway aligned with Targets 14 and 28; establish effective-conservation mechanisms such as zoning, conservation agreements, wetland management, and technical restrictions on drainage and burning in critical areas; implement territorial programs for sustainable-management practices on prioritized agricultural lands and grasslands, including agroforestry and silvopastoral systems, with technical assistance from MIDA/IDIAP and selection criteria to avoid unplanned agricultural expansion; operationalize a monitoring and verification system integrating coverage indicators and measurements/estimates of soil organic carbon with interoperable reporting with national systems under Targets 21 and 25; adjust and standardize conservation instruments and productive-practice packages based on implementation lessons from 2028-2030, defining scaling criteria, operational costs, and territorial capacity requirements; scale up protection/management coverage to new prioritized territories, prioritizing hydrological connectivity and critical landscapes, and expand adoption of soil practices on agricultural lands and grasslands; integrate criteria for protection of organic soils and increase of soil carbon into sectoral and local territorial and productive planning instruments; execute a national technical verification of progress and identify territorial gaps and causes; implement gap-closing measures in lagging territories, including adjustments to conservation instruments, reinforcement of technical assistance, and corrections of incentives driving wetland degradation or soil-carbon loss.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Organic soils, associated wetlands, peatlands, high-carbon soils, prioritized agricultural lands, grasslands, critical territories, critical landscapes, and hydrologically connected territories.",
"Target Audience": "MiAMBIENTE, MIDA, IDIAP (Panama Agricultural Research Institute), local governments, territorial actors, and actors involved in sectoral and local territorial and productive planning.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "A national operational definition and baseline for organic soils and associated wetlands; prioritized territories identified by risk and carbon/biodiversity value; effective-conservation instruments and sustainable-management practice packages adopted and standardized; monitoring and verification systems operational and interoperable with national systems; expanded protection/management coverage of organic soils and wetlands; increased adoption of sustainable practices on agricultural lands and grasslands; systematic integration of organic-soil protection and soil-carbon criteria into planning instruments; national technical verification of progress; and progress toward 70% of organic soils under effective protection/management and +10% soil organic carbon in prioritized agricultural lands and grasslands."
panama_HR_17:
"Goal/Purpose": "Transform agri-food systems in 21 priority districts through climate-smart and sustainable productive practices, ensuring coherence with adaptation, mitigation, and conservation targets.",
"Action/Intervention": "Define technical and climate criteria for selecting the 21 priority districts, considering climate vulnerability, pressure on ecosystems, productive importance, and local capacities; identify the most viable climate-smart productive practices within prioritized districts, including agroforestry, silvopastoral systems, sustainable aquaculture, and efficient soil and water management, aligned with the PNCCSA and MIDA policies; implement pilot agri-food transformation programs in prioritized districts with technical accompaniment, field validation, and participation of local producers; strengthen agricultural extension and technical assistance services using the capacities of MIDA, IDIAP, and technical partners; monitor adoption of practices, changes in productivity, resilience, and reduction of environmental pressures using existing agroclimatic and territorial information systems; evaluate pilot program results to identify the most effective practices, territories, and models; progressively scale up validated sustainable agri-food practices to new producers within prioritized districts, linking them with value chains and markets; integrate agri-food transformation into MIDA's sectoral policies and territorial plans.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Agri-food systems in prioritized districts within the agricultural sector.",
"Target Audience": "Local producers in the prioritized districts; MIDA; IDIAP; technical partners.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Adoption of sustainable practices; changes in productivity; increased resilience; reduction of environmental pressures; identification of practices, territories, and models with the greatest climate, productive, and social effectiveness; progressive scaling of validated practices to new producers within prioritized districts; integration of agri-food transformation into MIDA's sectoral policies and territorial plans."
panama_HR_18:
"Goal/Purpose": "Build an official national baseline of urban green and blue spaces valid for 2027; identify priority municipalities and neighborhoods for increasing urban green and blue spaces; incorporate green and blue infrastructure into Local Land-Use Plans; implement, monitor, manage, maintain, and scale up urban green and blue infrastructure; and ensure continuity of these actions beyond 2030 with guidance for expansion after 2035.",
"Action/Intervention": "Establish the methodology and first key indicators of coverage, access, and quality for a national baseline, articulating municipal, metropolitan, and sectoral information; define technical and social criteria to identify priority municipalities and neighborhoods considering climate vulnerability, deficit of green areas, and population density; establish national technical guidelines for incorporating green and blue infrastructure into Local Land-Use Plans aligned with the National Adaptation Plan for the Human Settlements Sector; explicitly integrate these criteria into the Local Land-Use Plans of prioritized municipalities and ensure formal adoption by local authorities; implement pilot interventions for the creation and recovery of parks, green corridors, urban wetlands, and sustainable drainage in prioritized neighborhoods; monitor the increase in urban green and blue space surface and its contribution to reducing climate vulnerability using territorial and climate-information systems; formalize municipal mechanisms for management and maintenance including institutional responsibilities, operational budgets, and community-participation schemes; scale up green and blue infrastructure solutions to new neighborhoods and municipalities while strengthening local government technical and management capacities; integrate evaluation results into updates of the National Adaptation Plan for the Human Settlements Sector and future urban-planning instruments; define technical guidelines for expansion after 2035.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Urban green and blue spaces; green and blue infrastructure; prioritized municipalities and neighborhoods; Local Land-Use Plans; Human Settlements Sector; urban planning and climate adaptation.",
"Target Audience": "National authorities responsible for the National Adaptation Plan for the Human Settlements Sector; local authorities in prioritized municipalities; local governments; municipal institutions responsible for management and maintenance; communities participating in sustainability schemes; prioritized neighborhoods.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "An official national reference on urban green and blue spaces valid for 2027; defined priority municipalities and neighborhoods; formal adoption of green and blue infrastructure criteria in Local Land-Use Plans of prioritized municipalities; pilot creation and recovery of urban green and blue spaces; monitored increase in the surface of urban green and blue spaces; contribution to reduction of climate vulnerability; formalized municipal management and maintenance mechanisms with responsibilities, budgets, and community participation; scaled-up solutions in additional neighborhoods and municipalities; integration of evaluation results into the next update cycle of the National Adaptation Plan for the Human Settlements Sector and urban-planning instruments; technical guidelines for expansion after 2035."
panama_HR_19:
"Goal/Purpose": "Define and implement a national framework of Multi-hazard Early Warning Systems, establish anticipatory-action protocols and financing mechanisms, and ensure effective coverage, accessibility, activation, and continuous improvement of the systems in 10 prioritized vulnerable regions.",
"Action/Intervention": "Define the national framework of Multi-hazard Early Warning Systems, including standards, institutional roles, information flows, and protocols for activating anticipatory actions; identify and prioritize 10 vulnerable regions based on climate exposure, social vulnerability, and local capacities; develop the draft EWS and Anticipatory Actions roadmap; integrate climate, hydrological, coastal, and territorial information; design anticipatory-action protocols linking warning levels with decisions, responsibilities, and preventive measures; design financing mechanisms for anticipatory action in coordination with Target 28; implement operational Multi-hazard Early Warning Systems in the 10 prioritized regions; activate mechanisms for anticipatory action and local financing; ensure accessibility of information through appropriate channels, languages, and formats; monitor and evaluate system performance and incorporate feedback.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Multi-hazard Early Warning Systems, anticipatory action, climate, hydrological, coastal, and territorial information, and vulnerable regions.",
"Target Audience": "Authorities, communities, producers, and local authorities.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Operational Multi-hazard Early Warning Systems implemented in 10 prioritized vulnerable regions; availability of anticipatory-action and local financing mechanisms before extreme events; effective coverage and use by authorities and communities; accessible information for communities, producers, and local authorities; and improved system accuracy, response times, and effectiveness through monitoring and evaluation."
panama_HR_20:
"Goal/Purpose": "Finalize and institutionalize climate resilience in the energy sector by incorporating climate scenarios, physical risks, and resilience criteria into energy planning, infrastructure design, system expansion, operation, maintenance, emergency response, and periodic review processes.",
"Action/Intervention": "Finalize the Adaptation Plan for the Energy Sector; review current energy-planning instruments to identify where and how climate scenarios, physical risks, and resilience criteria should be incorporated into expansion, operation, and maintenance decisions; define technical criteria of climate resilience for energy infrastructure, including risk thresholds, design standards, and adaptation priorities for extreme climate events; incorporate climate scenarios and physical-risk analysis into formal national energy planning processes; prioritize and implement adaptation measures in critical energy infrastructure exposed to elevated climate risks such as floods, droughts, and landslides; integrate the energy sector into national protocols for early warning and response to climate emergencies, with clear operational roles for generators, transmitters, and distributors; evaluate the energy system's performance during climate events using resilience indicators such as duration of interruptions, areas affected, and recovery times to adjust technical and operational criteria; integrate climate-resilience criteria permanently into the technical and regulatory framework of the energy sector so their application is mandatory in planning, operation, and maintenance; institutionalize a periodic mechanism for review and updating of climate resilience aligned with new climate scenarios and operational lessons.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Energy sector, including energy infrastructure for generation, transmission, and distribution, and national energy planning, operation, maintenance, and emergency-response systems.",
"Target Audience": "Generators, transmitters, distributors, national energy planners, and entities responsible for the technical and regulatory framework of the energy sector.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Energy planning and infrastructure decisions formally consider current and future climate vulnerabilities; technical and regulatory application of climate-resilience criteria becomes mandatory in system planning, operation, and maintenance; adaptation measures are implemented in critical infrastructure exposed to climate risks; the energy sector is integrated into early warning and emergency-response protocols with defined operational roles; and energy-system performance is evaluated through resilience indicators such as interruption duration, affected areas, and recovery times to support ongoing updates and adjustments."
panama_HR_21:
"Goal/Purpose": "Formalize OSIGA (Integrated Agroclimatic Management System Observatory) as the central national platform for agroclimatic information and ensure its use in territorial decisions, productive planning, risk management, adaptation planning, and agri-food-system transformation.",
"Action/Intervention": "Formalize the operational mandate of OSIGA, defining responsibilities, information flows, and inter-institutional coordination mechanisms; technically integrate the Climate Risk Atlas and other relevant systems into OSIGA, ensuring database interoperability, common standards, and periodic information updating; strengthen and standardize the operation of the Agroclimatic Technical Roundtables, defining clear protocols for the use of agroclimatic information in territorial decisions, productive planning, and risk management; integrate OSIGA as a mandatory input in the formulation and implementation of local and regional adaptation plans and agri-food-system transformation programs; strengthen OSIGA's interoperability with early-warning systems, adaptation-monitoring systems, and territorial observatories, ensuring bidirectional information flows; train territorial technicians and decision-makers in the systematic use of agroclimatic information for planning, investment, and response to extreme events.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Agroclimatic information systems, territorial planning, adaptation planning, risk management, and agri-food systems.",
"Target Audience": "OSIGA, inter-institutional actors involved in agroclimatic information management, Agroclimatic Technical Roundtables, territorial technicians, and decision-makers.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "OSIGA operates as the central national platform for agroclimatic information with defined responsibilities, interoperable databases, common standards, periodic information updates, standardized roundtable operations, mandatory use in local and regional adaptation plans and agri-food-system transformation programs, strengthened bidirectional information flows with related systems, and trained territorial technicians and decision-makers using agroclimatic information systematically for planning, investment, and response to extreme events."
panama_HR_22:
"Goal/Purpose": "Define and validate a standardized methodology for Local and Regional Adaptation Plans; identify and prioritize territories for plan development or updating; develop and formally integrate Local and Regional Adaptation Plans into local, regional, and watershed planning; implement priority adaptation actions; and channel financing for plan implementation.",
"Action/Intervention": "Define a standardized methodology for Local and Regional Adaptation Plans, including minimum contents, territorial prioritization criteria, participatory approach, gender integration, social safeguards, and alignment with development plans and watershed management; identify and prioritize territories based on climate vulnerability, ecological value, provision of ecosystem services, water-resource protection, presence of protected areas, coastal zones, and indigenous territories; articulate climate, risk, and territorial information from OSIGA, early-warning systems, and environmental monitoring; develop pilot adaptation plans in an initial group of prioritized territories; establish territorial governance arrangements for each pilot plan, defining roles of local governments, communities, traditional authorities, sectoral entities, and MiAMBIENTE; develop at least 8 Local and Regional Adaptation Plans in prioritized territories; formally integrate adaptation plans into local and regional development plans and watershed management plans; develop at least 4 Local and Regional Adaptation Plans in prioritized territories; implement priority adaptation actions identified in the plans, including nature-based solutions, risk management, productive adaptation, and strengthening of ecosystem services; channel specific financing for implementation using the mechanisms defined in Target 28 and aligning public, private, and cooperation resources.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Local and regional territories prioritized based on climate vulnerability, ecological value, ecosystem services, water-resource protection, protected areas, coastal zones, indigenous territories, and watershed management.",
"Target Audience": "Local governments, communities, traditional authorities, sectoral entities, MiAMBIENTE, and prioritized territories where local and regional adaptation plans will be developed or updated.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "A standardized methodology for Local and Regional Adaptation Plans is established and validated through pilot plans; prioritized territories are identified; territorial governance arrangements are established; at least 8 Local and Regional Adaptation Plans are developed in prioritized territories; at least 4 Local and Regional Adaptation Plans are developed in prioritized territories; adaptation plans are formally integrated into local, regional, and watershed management plans with binding character; priority adaptation actions are implemented; and financing is channeled for implementation."
panama_HR_23:
"Goal/Purpose": "Publish the Marine-Coastal Adaptation Plan and articulate marine-coastal adaptation with local planning, ensuring coherence with the Local and Regional Adaptation Plans (Target 22) and coastal-development plans.",
"Action/Intervention": "Establish local governance arrangements for implementation, defining the roles of local governments, coastal communities, traditional authorities, MiAMBIENTE, and other sectoral entities; implement marine-coastal adaptation interventions with Nature-based Solutions in prioritized zones, prioritizing the restoration of mangroves, dunes, and coastal wetlands, and strengthening natural protection in the face of extreme events and sea-level rise; integrate coastal-adaptation measures into the management of the marine SINAP, ensuring coherence among conservation, restoration, and climate-risk reduction; channel specific financing for marine-coastal adaptation using the mechanisms defined in Target 28 and aligning public, private, and cooperation resources.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Marine-coastal areas, prioritized coastal zones, mangroves, dunes, coastal wetlands, and the marine SINAP.",
"Target Audience": "Local governments, coastal communities, traditional authorities, MiAMBIENTE, and other sectoral entities.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Coherent marine-coastal adaptation planning and implementation; restoration of mangroves, dunes, and coastal wetlands; strengthened natural protection against extreme events and sea-level rise; integration of coastal-adaptation measures into marine SINAP management; and mobilization of specific financing for marine-coastal adaptation."
panama_HR_24:
"Goal/Purpose": "Finalize the National Adaptation Plan for the Health Sector and integrate climate information into national epidemiological surveillance and health decision-making, ensuring continuity and improvement of the climate-health approach beyond 2030.",
"Action/Intervention": "Precisely define the priority climate variables to be incorporated into national epidemiological surveillance; design a national methodology for integrating climate information into epidemiological surveillance systems, establishing roles, information flows, and use criteria for health decisions; incorporate climate variables and projections into the epidemiological surveillance systems of prioritized health facilities, ensuring interoperability with climate- and risk-information systems; train health personnel in the use of climate information for prevention, early detection, and response to climate-sensitive health risks, prioritizing regions of high vulnerability; formalize sectoral protocols for using integrated climate and epidemiological information to activate preventive measures, contingency plans, and inter-institutional coordination; expand climate-health integration to the rest of the public health network, ensuring methodological consistency and data quality in at least 80% of health facilities; integrate climate-sensitive health indicators into national systems for adaptation and loss-and-damage monitoring, guaranteeing periodic reporting; incorporate evaluation results into updates of sectoral health and adaptation plans.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Health sector, national epidemiological surveillance systems, public health network, adaptation and loss-and-damage monitoring systems.",
"Target Audience": "Health personnel, prioritized health facilities, the rest of the public health network, and institutions involved in epidemiological surveillance, climate information, risk information, adaptation monitoring, and inter-institutional coordination.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Climate variables and projections are incorporated into epidemiological surveillance systems; interoperability with climate- and risk-information systems is ensured; health personnel are trained in the use of climate information; sectoral protocols are formalized for preventive measures, contingency plans, and coordination; climate-health integration is expanded with methodological consistency and data quality in at least 80% of health facilities; climate-sensitive health indicators are periodically reported in national adaptation and loss-and-damage monitoring systems; evaluation results are incorporated into updated sectoral health and adaptation plans."
panama_HR_25:
"Goal/Purpose": "Strengthen and operationalize climate adaptation and Loss and Damage monitoring, evaluation, data governance, interoperability, transparency, and planned relocation procedures for decision-making and public transparency.",
"Action/Intervention": "Formalize institutional agreements on data flow per indicator, prioritizing indicators with yellow/red traffic-light status and those most used in public decision-making; develop the draft regulatory framework for the Planned Relocation protocol; install a universal data-collection scheme with field templates and an interoperable repository to reduce duplication and standardize climate-change and Loss and Damage variables; finalize the Loss and Damage section in the PNTC; design the climate-displacement component including cooperation and data-flow agreements, event typology, minimum variables, and reporting pathway; evaluate the functionality of the Adaptation M&E system and the Loss and Damage subsystem with external technical cooperation, including gap analysis, interoperability, roles, sustainability, and costs; improve data source and quality through cleansing of series, validation rules, quality control, and an annual recalculation cycle with data providers; issue or adopt the Ministerial Resolution on technical aspects, or ensure its effective implementation through manuals, leads, schedule, and institutional compliance; operate the M&E Module in the PNTC with recalculation executed by data providers, annual calendar, cross-validation, and publication; achieve interoperability with the Risk Observatory through a shared data dictionary, API/ETL, and a joint risk-measures-results-L&D dashboard; implement pilot projects to evaluate the effectiveness of measures versus the quantification of Loss and Damage by sector or territory, including equipment and evaluation methodology; operationalize the Planned Relocation Protocol including last alternative criteria, pathway of rights, livelihoods and services, institutional roles, and financing mechanisms; publish the annual M&E dashboard for adaptation and Loss and Damage with updated information.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Climate change adaptation, Loss and Damage, climate displacement, planned relocation, monitoring and evaluation systems, data management and interoperability, public decision-making, and transparency platforms including the PNTC and Risk Observatory.",
"Target Audience": "Institutions responsible for indicator data flows, data providers, institutions required to comply with the Ministerial Resolution, the PNTC and Risk Observatory, external technical cooperation actors, and public decision-makers.",
